title: Concern groups
description: The eight semantic concerns a subgraph is grouped by, inside every subgraph TYPOLOGY that groups at all (skills, processes, schemas, tests, library, uml): `<kind dir>/<group>/`. Owner, 2026-09-29: "declared sub-graphs of cat-harness based on semantic concern … dont need a separate facet. built into location." Ruled 2026-09-30: eight groups (bean 9umr). A group id is SHARED: every instance and every kind uses these eight, the harness declares each group once from within the kind's own declaration file, and a higher instance's same-named directory is a named MEMBER of it (bean 1g4s, option A) — so a higher instance adds no group of its own. The vocabulary lives here ONCE, as a code list, so the declaration files name groups by code and restate nothing (placement proposal §1.1; AGENTS.md "one fact, one place"). Checked by `check:concern-groups`.

source.note: Bean folio-assistant-9umr, owner rulings 2026-09-29 and 2026-09-30; placement proposal §1.2 (bean folio-assistant-ejye, PR0).

codes.label: Software delivery lifecycle
codes.definition: How a change is planned, tracked, verified and shipped: the work plan (beans), branches, PRs, CI and gates, QA and adjudication, staging, and release.

codes.label: Process model and execution
codes.definition: How work is modelled and run: BPMN and DMN, roles and task authorization, workflow-engine state, and the methodologies a process adopts (RACI, CRDM, spec-kit, SWOT, Kepner-Tregoe, MADR).

codes.label: Tools and MCP
codes.definition: How a capability becomes a Tool node and an MCP service, and how that service is deployed and authenticated. A tool may describe its OWN specific subprocesses beside it, so a general skill is not bogged down by one tool's detail (owner, 2026-09-30).

codes.label: Knowledge graph
codes.definition: How the graph is declared, placed, read, restructured, exported and audited, including skill registration and placement.

codes.label: Library and information management
codes.definition: How a source is acquired, uploaded, described by metadata in the KG, and held in library/. The harness holds the basic flow; core holds the detailed methods.

codes.label: Content authoring
codes.definition: How content is authored, reviewed, validated and published, independent of content type (lifecycle, voice review, technical writing). Higher instances put their content-type packages here.

codes.label: Rendering, UI and publication surfaces
codes.definition: How the corpus is rendered, published and presented: the docs site, viewers, boards and themes.

codes.label: Agent conduct
codes.definition: How an agent behaves: interaction, confirmation, memory, reporting, swarms and security.
